sections.content: How many people are "management consultants and business analysts"?

119,240 people

were counted on the census as "management consultants and business analysts" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Management consultants and business analysts advise industrial, commercial and other establishments on a variety of management and business-related matters to assist in the formulation of financial and business policies in order to maximise growth or improve business performance.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "management consultants and business analysts" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "management consultants and business analysts", 14.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "management consultants and business analysts" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "management consultants and business analysts" included:

  • conservation professionals
  • business associate professionals (other)
  • engineering professionals (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "management consultants and business analysts" there were more men than women (61.6% compared with 38.4%).

This means "management consultants and business analysts" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 61.6% and women made up 38.4% of "management consultants and business analysts"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "management consultants and business analysts" included:

  • assemblers (electrical and electronic products)
  • sales accounts and business development managers
  • functional managers and directors (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "management consultants and business analysts" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "management consultants and business analysts" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "management consultants and business analysts", 7.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (82.8% compared with 17.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (77%) than self-employed (23%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wandsworth, this is in the same region of London.
